events.title: OIC 1222/1967 divides the Province into 27 areas for regional hospital districts under section 3 of the Regional Hospital Districts Act (SBC 1967 c.43)

evidence.locator: OIC 1222/1967, approved and ordered 13 April 1967; recital of s.3 and schedule of areas 1-27 (PDF pp. 1-3); recommended by the acting Minister of Health Services and Hospital Insurance (signature block, PDF p. 3)

events.interpretation_notes: The day the order defining the areas was approved. It is not a common incorporation date: each district was incorporated later by its own letters patent (the 28 originals recovered run from 29 June 1967, Greater Vancouver, to 8 October 1968, Squamish-Lillooet). The department recommended the order; the districts are local corporations with their own boards, not branches of the department, and are not drawn as bodies.

events.title: OIC 3082/1969 dissolves 23 hospital improvement districts incorporated under the Water Act and transfers all their assets, rights, claims, obligations and liabilities to the regional hospital district paired with each

evidence.locator: OIC 3082/1969, approved and ordered 25 September 1969; recitals, operative recommendation under s.50C of the Regional Hospital Districts Act, and Schedule columns A-B; recommended by the Minister of Health Services and Hospital Insurance

events.interpretation_notes: The order recites that the hospital fund-raising functions of the improvement districts had been assigned to the regional hospital districts. Dissolution and transfer take effect by the order itself. The 23 districts were incorporated by letters patent between 7 August 1951 (Creston Valley) and 23 April 1964 (Kelowna and District); this is the recovered set, not a census of every hospital improvement district. Fort Nelson (13 June 1972) and 100 Mile House (12 May 1972) were dissolved by later orders and are not part of this one.

events.title: OIC 527/1972 amends the letters patent of 28 regional hospital districts so that their municipal membership, electoral areas and voting units follow the corresponding municipal regional districts

evidence.locator: OIC 527/1972, approved and ordered 8 February 1972; recitals and Schedule A; recommended by the Minister of Health Services and Hospital Insurance

events.interpretation_notes: The approval day of a coordinating amendment to existing corporations, not 28 new incorporations. A later recital (OIC 245/2021) that calls this the letters-patent date of Skeena-Queen Charlotte does not reset that district's 17 August 1967 start. The recitals describe boards of corresponding regional directors; each district's first board is in its own letters patent.

events.title: Fraser Valley Regional Hospital District incorporated by letters patent amalgamating the Central Fraser Valley, Dewdney-Alouette and Fraser-Cheam regional hospital districts, which are dissolved at midnight at the end of 11 December 1995

evidence.locator: OIC 1501/1995, approved and ordered 7 December 1995; order paras. 1-4 and letters patent (recitals under Hospital District Act s.5, "on and from December 12, 1995"); recommended by the Minister of Health and Minister Responsible for Seniors

events.interpretation_notes: The effective day of the new letters patent; the order was approved on 7 December. The district comprises the Fraser Valley Regional District established the same day under the Municipal Act. This hospital district is not the Fraser Valley Health Region (a health board drawn in the atlas); the two are different legal bodies.

events.title: OIC 1549/1995 limits 24 regional hospital districts, from 31 December 1995, to completing minister-approved capital projects, paying their debt, requisitioning and any other power the minister approves

evidence.locator: OIC 1549/1995, approved and ordered 14 December 1995; Schedule A, paragraph added to each district's letters patent ("Effective December 31, 1995 ... shall not exercise any powers ... except")

events.interpretation_notes: The effective day of the restriction; the order was approved on 14 December. A restriction of powers, not a dissolution: the districts continued, thirteen had the restriction repealed on 19 November 1998, and others were dissolved one by one between 2000 and 2025.

events.title: Twelve new regional hospital districts incorporated by letters patent: Cariboo, Central Vancouver Island, Coast Garibaldi, East Kootenay, Northern Interior, North Okanagan, North West, Peace Liard, South Okanagan Similkameen, Thompson, Upper Island/Central Coast and West Kootenay-Boundary

evidence.locator: OIC 1550/1995 to OIC 1561/1995 (one order per district), each approved 14 December 1995; final clause of each letters patent ("The effective date of these Letters Patent is January 1, 1996"). URL is OIC 1550/1995 (Cariboo); the other eleven are at arc_oic/1551_1995 to 1561_1995

events.interpretation_notes: Incorporation in force 1 January 1996; 14 December 1995 is the approval day, not the start. The new Cariboo, East Kootenay and North Okanagan districts are separate corporations from the 1967-68 districts of the same names, which continued under the 1995 restriction. Several share names with regional health boards of 1994-95 (Northern Interior, Thompson, Central Vancouver Island and others); a hospital district is not a health board, and no identity is drawn between them.

events.title: OIC 1429/1998 repeals the 1995 restriction for 13 older regional hospital districts, orders five of the 1996 districts dissolved on 31 December 1998 with their assets divided among named districts, and continues Cariboo-Coast as Cariboo-Chilcotin and Coast Garibaldi as Sea to Sky with smaller territory

evidence.locator: OIC 1429/1998, approved and ordered 19 November 1998; Schedule A ss.1,3,4,7-12,16,18,19,21 (restrictions repealed), ss.5,15,17,20,22 (dissolutions and transfers), ss.2 and 6 (renames and partial transfers), ss.13,14,23 (membership and boundaries)

events.interpretation_notes: The day of the order. Restored powers are not new incorporations. Transfers had to be completed by 31 December 1998, and the schedule makes vesting depend on each actual transfer; the closing days are not recovered. The renames take effect immediately. OIC 1430/1998 separately incorporated the Stuart-Nechako Regional Hospital District on the same day.

events.title: Central Vancouver Island, Northern Interior, Peace Liard, South Okanagan Similkameen and Upper Island/Central Coast regional hospital districts, incorporated 1 January 1996, dissolved
events.interpretation_notes: The dissolution day the order sets. It is also the deadline for transferring their assets to the named districts, not proof that each transfer was executed that day. These hospital districts are not the regional health boards or community health services societies of similar names.

events.title: OIC 1601/1998 dissolves the Greater Vancouver Regional Hospital District and transfers its assets: 15 acres in Surrey to the South Fraser Health Region, the Tilbury Laundry and adjacent land to the Vancouver/Richmond Health Board, a parkade to Vancouver General Hospital, and the rest of its assets and liabilities to the government

evidence.locator: OIC 1601/1998, approved and ordered 17 December 1998; order paras. 1-2, Appendix ss.1-6 and Schedules A-D; authority: Hospital District Act s.2 and Greater Vancouver Transportation Authority Act, SBC 1998 c.30

events.interpretation_notes: Effective 1 January 1999; approved 17 December 1998. Four recipient groups, not a merger into one health body. The Surrey land returns to the government unless an independent review within three years shows it is needed for health programs; the parkade vests in the government if Vancouver General Hospital pays its operating costs or debt from health-program funds or misses the Schedule D payments. Whether either reversion happened is not known. The district was incorporated 29 June 1967 (OIC 2131/1967).

events.title: OIC 3240/1977 orders a proclamation bringing the Ministerial Titles Amendment Act, 1977 into force, except listed provisions

evidence.locator: OIC 3240/1977, approved and ordered 21 October 1977; operative clause and exceptions (a)-(e)

events.interpretation_notes: The order that a proclamation issue, not the proclamation. The exceptions are provisions of the Liquor Control and Licensing, Mineral, Public Schools, Soil Conservation, Special Provincial Employment Programmes, Municipalities Aid and Trade-schools Regulation Acts. The issued proclamation and its Gazette publication are not retrieved. The Act's assent (27 September 1977) is already held.

events.title: The official 1994 Table of Statutes records the Ministerial Titles Amendment Act, 1977 (c.75) amendments to the Hospital Corporations Act (ss.2, 5 and 10) as proclaimed in force 21 October 1977

evidence.locator: 1994 Table of Statutes, Hospital Corporations Act entry, printed p.1022 (PDF p.90); also West Coast National Park Act s.7, printed p.1198 (PDF p.266)

events.interpretation_notes: Corroboration from an official compilation for these provisions only. It is not a direct entry for the retitling of the Department of Health Act, and not proof that every provision of the 1977 Act came into force that day; the proclamation itself is still missing.

not_applied.subject: The 28 original regional hospital districts, incorporated 29 June 1967 to 8 October 1968

local_register_proposal.what: A register of local hospital-finance corporations, read by no diagram build, so the atlas can cite them in events and lineage without drawing them as provincial bodies.
local_register_proposal.proposed_file: research/history/local-hospital-districts.json (schema local-hospital-districts/1), generated from round4/root/hospital_districts.json and hospital_improvement_districts.json by a convert.py in the review folder
local_register_proposal.why_not_health_authority: health-authority is used for bodies that govern or deliver health services under the Health Authorities Act or the 2001 regulation, and that answer to the Ministry of Health. A regional hospital district raises and repays hospital capital through requisitions on its member municipalities and electoral areas. Its board is made up of regional-district directors, and the minister approves its capital spending. A hospital improvement district was a Water Act improvement district with elected trustees. Neither runs a hospital, and no source in the module says that either answered to a ministry.
